rewrites.title: AP-1 motif mutation at persistent enhancers with feedback-loop modeling
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at enhancers that stay open after stimulation, then measure persistence of chromatin marks and gene expression. Fit a bistable feedback model (AP-1 inducing its own enhancers and chromatin remodelers) to the data, to test whether memory requires the positive feedback loop or only an epigenetic mark that AP-1 deposits.

rewrites.title: Decoupling AP-1 occupancy from its chromatin trace
rewrites.description: After a transient stimulus, run parallel time courses of AP-1 protein levels (FOS/JUN immunofluorescence, degron-tagged reporters) and of chromatin state at AP-1 motifs (ATAC-seq, FOS/JUN CUT&RUN, H3K27ac). Memory is supported only if accessibility and enhancer marks persist long after AP-1 occupancy has decayed.

rewrites.title: Re-stimulation of primed versus naive cells with AP-1 motif mutation
rewrites.description: Compare the first and second responses to the same stimulus, measuring AP-1 target induction, Pol II loading, and enhancer accessibility. Memory predicts faster or stronger re-induction in previously stimulated cells. Also mutate AP-1 motifs at the primed enhancers with CRISPR to test whether the memory depends on those specific sites.

rewrites.title: Prime–rest–rechallenge with windowed AP-1 degradation
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (serum, TGF-β, wounding, or drug), allow full return to baseline transcriptome, then restimulate days later and quantify whether the secondary response is faster, larger, or qualitatively different. Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on FOS/JUN to remove AP-1 selectively during the priming window, the rest (storage) window, or the recall window, to distinguish whether AP-1 acts as the writer, maintainer, or reader of the memory.

rewrites.title: Dual-pulse live imaging of transcriptional bursting at single-allele resolution
rewrites.description: Knock MS2/PP7 cassettes into AP-1 target genes and live-image transcriptional bursting across a priming pulse, a rest interval, and a second pulse. Test whether memory appears as shortened latency, higher burst frequency, or reduced cell-to-cell variance, and whether the same alleles that fired first fire again, establishing allele-level rather than only cell-level memory.

rewrites.title: MPRA of AP-1 enhancer motif syntax
rewrites.description: Build an integrated massively parallel reporter library varying AP-1 motif number, spacing, affinity, and flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, lineage factors). Measure which configurations sustain elevated output after stimulus withdrawal, to determine whether memory resides in AP-1 sites alone or in their sequence context.

rewrites.title: Site-specific perturbation of AP-1 motifs and neighboring chromatin state
rewrites.description: In primed cells, use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at selected enhancers, or use dCas9 to recruit or block AP-1 there. Test whether the enhancers' memory-linked accessibility and faster re-induction depend on the motif. Also use dCas9-based editing of neighboring chromatin marks to test whether AP-1 acts through those marks or independently of them.

rewrites.title: Heritable lineage recording of AP-1 activity history
rewrites.description: Drive a stable reporter (Cre-loxP switch, or a CRISPR-based cumulative recorder) from AP-1-responsive enhancers so that each past AP-1 activation leaves a permanent, heritable mark. Sort or image cells by mark and track their clonal descendants, to test whether prior AP-1 activity is inherited through divisions and predicts later responses.

rewrites.title: Primed versus naive re-stimulation kinetics
rewrites.description: Compare first and second exposures to the same stimulus after a rest period, measuring the timing, amplitude, and recruitment speed of AP-1 binding and target gene transcription (nascent RNA-seq, qPCR time courses). A memory mechanism predicts faster and stronger responses on re-exposure, and this advantage should disappear when AP-1 binding sites are mutated.

rewrites.title: Heritable barcoding to measure how long memory survives mitosis
rewrites.description: Heritably barcode single cells (Watermelon/CellTag plus single-cell multiome), stimulate, allow several divisions, then restimulate and ask whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction propagate down clonal trees. The key measurement is the decay constant of sister- and cousin-cell correlation in AP-1 site accessibility as a function of generation number, distinguishing true inheritance from stochastic resampling.

rewrites.title: Timed AP-1 degradation to separate establishment from maintenance
rewrites.description: Remove AP-1 acutely at different times (during induction, versus after the memory state is established) using degrons or inducible dominant negatives. If AP-1 is needed only to establish memory, the state persists after loss; if it is also needed to maintain it, the state decays. This separates initiation from maintenance and from epigenetic carriers such as histone marks.

rewrites.title: Allele-resolved AP-1 reporters
rewrites.description: Use SNP-resolved allele-specific RNA FISH or dual-color knock-in reporters at the two alleles of an AP-1 target (e.g., AXL, SERPINE1) to test whether the same allele remains the high-expressing one across days and through cell division. Allele-autonomous, cis-restricted persistence implies chromatin-encoded memory rather than a diffusible trans-factor set point.

rewrites.title: MPRA of AP-1 motif syntax under stimulus–washout–restimulus
rewrites.description: Build a synthetic reporter library systematically varying TRE/CRE motif number, spacing, affinity, and flanking partner motifs (TEAD, RUNX, CEBP, nucleosome-positioning sequences). Measure each variant's output after a single stimulus versus a stimulus–washout–restimulus protocol, to identify which cis-regulatory arrangements confer memory (faster, larger, or lower-threshold second responses) rather than mere responsiveness.

rewrites.title: Stimulus–washout–restimulus ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN time course
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (e.g. with serum, TPA or an inflammatory signal), wash out the stimulus, and rest them for days. Profile chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and H3K27ac by CUT&RUN. Restimulate and compare the transcriptional response with that of naive cells. Persistent open sites that carry AP-1 motifs and give faster or stronger induction would support memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome and live reporter lineage tracing
rewrites.description: Combine single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing with live-cell imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter (or endogenous tagged FOS) across cell divisions. Track whether daughter cells inherit the primed state, which would show mitotic heritability. Use the data to ask whether memory is a bistable, all-or-none state or a graded one, and to assess cell-to-cell variability in it.

rewrites.title: Dose-timing and delay-dependent recall assay
rewrites.description: Pre-stimulate with varying doses and durations, then re-challenge after increasing delays and fit the decay of the primed response to estimate memory half-life and recall strength. Repeat with DNA-binding-deficient or site-mutant AP-1 at the memory enhancers; a memory mediated by AP-1 should be abolished or shortened in these mutants.

rewrites.title: Acute degron depletion during induction versus maintenance
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/AID degrons on FOS, JUN or other AP-1 members and remove AP-1 either during stimulation or only after the stimulus has ended. This distinguishes whether AP-1 is required only for establishing accessibility or continuously for maintaining it. Read out chromatin state and faster transcription on secondary challenge.

rewrites.title: Primed versus naive re-stimulation response across rest intervals
rewrites.description: Compare transcriptional response magnitude and speed to a second stimulus in primed versus naive cells at varying rest intervals, using RNA-seq and single-cell readouts. Plot memory decay against rest time, and ask whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers show faster or stronger induction and whether an AP-1 dominant-negative (e.g., A-FOS) expressed only during priming abolishes the enhanced second response.

rewrites.title: Re-exposure kinetics with motif-mutant enhancers
rewrites.description: Compare first- and second-exposure transcriptional kinetics (e.g., nascent RNA by TT-seq or smFISH) at endogenous loci, wild-type versus CRISPR-edited TGAGTCA (TRE) motifs in the enhancers. A memory role predicts faster or stronger second responses that disappear when the AP-1 site is mutated, while priming that is not memory would not depend on the motif.

rewrites.title: Stimulus-withdrawal time course with AP-1 and chromatin readouts
rewrites.description: Pulse cells with a stimulus (e.g., TPA or growth factor), withdraw it, and track AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun), ATAC-seq, and H3K27ac at target enhancers over days. Memory requires these marks to persist after AP-1 protein and mRNA return to baseline.
